heroHeadline: UN Security Council Holds Emergency Session on Kenscoff Massacre as Hostage Crisis Drags On; Second Deportation Flight in a Week Lands 161 in Cap-Haïtien
heroSubtitle: Viv Ansanm coalition gunmen stormed Kenscoff on the night of August 23, 2026, torching roughly 25 homes and executing dozens inside a church sheltering earlier IDPs; the UN confirmed August 26 that the toll had risen to at least 47 killed, including 5+ children, with more than 50 people kidnapped — one of Haiti's largest mass-kidnapping incidents in recent years. A gang leader posted a hostage video threatening to kill captives if security forces moved against the gang and warned National Police Director Vladimir Paraison against continued drone strikes. By August 27, Kenscoff residents were demanding the local police chief's resignation over Paraison's discredited claim of a 66% violence reduction, police confirmed a threat to attack Tabarre (the US embassy neighborhood), and a second deportation flight in a week — 161 people removed from the US and the Bahamas, none former TPS holders — landed at Cap-Haïtien International Airport, adding pressure on the gang-besieged south. The UN Security Council convened an emergency session August 28, where Special Representative Carlos Ruiz Massieu confirmed 'three boys and two girls' among the Kenscoff dead, cited 1,408 people killed and 656 injured April–June alone, and urged faster activation of Haiti's specialized judicial units; members pressed for the Gang Suppression Force's acceleration toward its full 5,500-person mandate, with Chad and Mongolia having signed troop agreements and talks continuing with Jamaica, Sri Lanka, and Bangladesh. As of August 29, no hostage rescue had been reported and police continued declining to disclose operational plans.
